cases.name: named_vfs_read_control
cases.observed: SQLite opened the synthetic source through the non-default named VFS and returned the fixture marker.
cases.exact_object_identity: Not captured by the supported adapter; no inode/descriptor registration is claimed.

cases.name: named_vfs_write_refusal
cases.observed: An UPDATE through the supported named VFS failed because its xOpen refuses the main-journal role (SQLite reports SQLITE_NOMEM); the marker remained unchanged.
cases.exact_object_identity: Not captured; refusal is an adapter capability limit, not an identity-bound authorization decision.

cases.name: wal_shm_stop_condition
cases.observed: The named read-only VFS reported journal mode delete for a WAL request; the requested WAL mode was not selected. Neither WAL nor SHM fixture appeared in this read-only attempt; this does not prove an xShmMap interception.
cases.exact_object_identity: SHM identity was not exposed before SQLite's native SHM path; no xShmMap protection is claimed.
fixture_effects: WAL and SHM fixture paths absent after attempt

cases.name: backup_plain_destination_control
cases.observed: NewBackup's plain destination succeeded via SQLite's independently selected default VFS; source named-VFS selection did not protect it.
cases.exact_object_identity: Destination object was not opened through the named adapter; identity was not registered.

cases.name: backup_named_destination_refusal_and_fresh_retry
cases.observed: Explicit named-VFS backup destinations failed on the first attempt and a separate fresh retry; no protected backup bytes were written.
cases.exact_object_identity: No destination identity was captured; the adapter rejected its create/open path before a destination file appeared.
fixture_effects: first destination created=false then removed if present
the plain default-VFS control backup remains fixture-only and outside the named adapter boundary

conclusion: The pinned driver supports non-default read-only VFS selection and SQLite demonstrates independent backup destination routing. A no-fork writable exact-object pre-write adapter and pre-native SHM protection were not demonstrated; writable Token Logger coverage remains unsupported.
limitations: The supported modernc.org/sqlite/vfs adapter is read-only; no writable callback adapter was implemented.
No exact native descriptor was registered before SQLite writes; the experiment cannot establish a write barrier.
WAL/SHM acceptance is unavailable. A named read-only VFS refusal is not proof of a pre-native xShmMap interception.
The plain backup destination is an intentionally unprotected control and is confined to this disposable fixture.
This prototype does not cover Token Logger, concurrent external actors, rotation, production integration, or non-Linux behavior.
